subject: HIPAA BAA eligibility & deployment modes - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@healthcloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: HIPAA BAA eligibility & deployment modes - next steps

Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery on HIPAA/PHI handling and proposed next steps so your procurement and security teams have what they need.

Recap (from our call):
- HealthCloud will process limited PHI (patient names, DOB, limited identifiers) as part of clinical note enrichment.
- You require a signed BAA and evidence of controls (SOC 2) prior to production.
- Preferred deployment mode: customer-managed VPC/private deployment to keep PHI within your cloud account; Dedicated reserved capacity is also acceptable if VPC is not feasible.

Where we stand (Redwood):
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation. We can share the report under an NDA / secure link (see attachments).
- BAA: We have a standard BAA and can sign for Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment modes. Hosted/public API access is generally not HIPAA-eligible unless we put a dedicated private tenancy and specific contractual controls in place — we can discuss exceptions but plan for Dedicated or Private for PHI.
- PHI handling: For HIPAA-eligible deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can limit persistence/retention of request logs/KV cache.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will send our draft BAA and a short HIPAA deployment overview + standard answers to vendor security questionnaires (attached).
2) Samir: please share your vendor security questionnaire and confirm expected throughput (requests per minute) and retention window for clinical notes.
3) Rishi / Neha: internal follow-up to confirm technical details (KMS options, network controls, SOC 2 evidence we can share).

Timeline: if we can get the VSA back this week and confirm deployment mode, we should be able to get a signed BAA within ~2 weeks (legal review permitting).

Attaching: Redwood_BAA_Draft_20261101.pdf (draft), Redwood_HIPAA_Deployment_Overview.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Link.txt

Thanks — happy to set a follow-up call with Rishi and Neha for technical Q&A.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Samir Gupta <samir@healthcloud.com>

Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HIPAA BAA eligibility & deployment modes - next steps

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few notes and requests from our side:

1) We do need a BAA and prefer a VPC/private deployment so that PHI never traverses a shared tenancy. Dedicated reserved capacity in our account would also work if that is your recommended path.
2) I've attached our vendor security questionnaire (VSA) — it has a lot of technical-control questions (KMS, key rotation, network segmentation, audit logs, MFA, RBAC). Can your security team fill this out?
3) For encryption: we prefer customer-managed KMS from our cloud provider. Can you confirm Redwood supports CMKs for Private deployments?
4) Timeline: we are aiming for a Q4 pilot (late Dec) with production in Q1. Legal would like to review the BAA and SOC 2 evidence before committing.

Quick answers while we wait on your docs: expected throughput (pilot) ~200 reqs/minute, burst to 1,000 reqs/minute. Retention: we'd like logs/inputs stored no longer than 30 days, if possible.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looping in Legal to the thread.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: HIPAA BAA eligibility & deployment modes - next steps (internal)

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the heads up and attaching their VSA. Quick internal notes / recommended action items before we send formal responses:

1) SOC 2 evidence: we can share the SOC 2 Type II PDF under a secure link (requires access control). I'll generate the access token and redact any customer-specific items if legal requests it.
2) BAA: our standard BAA is fine for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem). We should check Legal on the data-subprocessor clause (HealthCloud will want clarity on subcontractors).
3) KMS/Encryption: for Private (VPC) we support customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK). Rishi: please confirm the exact KMS integration steps and any constraints on key rotation frequency.
4) PHI boundary & retention: we should offer a configuration to disable retention of request logs and to truncate KV cache for HIPAA workloads. Rishi, can you draft the technical note on retention controls and recommended defaults for 30-day retention?
5) Network controls: we need to provide an architecture diagram showing VPC peering/private endpoints and optional firewall rules.

Action items: Rishi to complete technical answers on KMS, retention, and network architecture (deliverable: Redwood_HIPAA_Deployment_Overview.pdf). Marissa to route BAA to Legal for signature and to send the initial filled VSA answers (or partial) back to HealthCloud. Neha to assemble SOC 2 link and escalation path for any redline requests.

I can turn around the SOC 2 access link and the high-level deployment overview by EOD tomorrow.

-Neha
